references.text: The Levite man refused to spend the night in a foreign city and instead chose Gibeah, an Israelite city, which sets the context for their arrival.
Lot sat at the gate of Sodom and invited the strangers in, in contrast to Gibeah where no one offered hospitality.
Abraham showed exemplary hospitality toward strangers, in sharp contrast to the people of Gibeah who did not welcome the travelers.
Jesus teaches about the importance of welcoming strangers, highlighting the sin of those who refused hospitality in Gibeah.
Gibeah is mentioned as a city in the tribe of Benjamin, the same geographical area where the event in Judges 19 takes place.
The exhortation not to forget hospitality stands in contrast to the people of Gibeah, who showed no hospitality.
